components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 她的情人每天都给她写信。
example.pinyin: Tā de qíngrén měitiān dōu gěi tā xiě xìn.
example.english: Her lover writes to her every day.
example.fact: 情人 pairs 情 ("feeling," built on the heart radical 忄) with 人 ("person"), but unlike the neutral 男朋友/女朋友 ("boyfriend/girlfriend"), it carries a stronger, sometimes illicit romantic charge — closer to English "lover" than to "significant other" — which is also why 情人节 ("Valentine's Day") reaches for this word rather than a plainer one.

examples.hanzi: 他和他的情人在海边散步。
examples.pinyin: Tā hé tā de qíngrén zài hǎibiān sànbù.
examples.english: He and his lover are strolling by the sea.

examples.hanzi: 情人节那天，餐厅里坐满了情人。
examples.pinyin: Qíngrénjié nàtiān, cāntīng lǐ zuò mǎn le qíngrén.
examples.english: On Valentine's Day, the restaurant was full of lovers.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
典 — a book 冊 set on a stand 丌, a revered text; hence canon, classic, as in 经典 classic and 字典 dictionary.

example.hanzi: 这部电影已经成为经典。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng yǐjīng chéngwéi jīngdiǎn.
example.english: This movie has already become a classic.
example.fact: 经 originally referred to the vertical warp threads in weaving before extending to mean "canon, scripture," while 典 pictures a bundle of bamboo strips — an ancient book — held up by two hands. 经典 fuses two separate words for "authoritative text" into one compound meaning "classic."

examples.hanzi: 这是一首经典的老歌。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì shǒu jīngdiǎn de lǎo gē.
examples.english: This is a classic old song.

examples.hanzi: 他们每年都会重看这部经典的电影。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen měi nián dōu huì chóng kàn zhè bù jīngdiǎn de diànyǐng.
examples.english: They rewatch this classic movie every year.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤; water means life: 活 is alive.
舌 (shé, tongue) is a loose sound clue for huó; also in 话 huà.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 年轻人充满活力。
example.pinyin: Niánqīng rén chōngmǎn huólì.
example.english: Young people are full of energy.
example.fact: 活 (water radical 氵 + phonetic 舌) evokes life as something flowing and unstill, while 力 depicts the blade of a plow, the ancient symbol of physical exertion — together 活力 paints vitality as flowing strength rather than mere existence.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市充满了活力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì chōngmǎn le huólì.
examples.english: This city is full of vitality.

examples.hanzi: 早上跑步让我一整天都有活力。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang pǎobù ràng wǒ yì zhěng tiān dōu yǒu huólì.
examples.english: Running in the morning gives me energy all day.

components.note: 父 (father) — a hand holding a stone axe, an image of the household head who works and rules.

example.hanzi: 他和父亲一起去钓鱼。
example.pinyin: Tā hé fùqīn yìqǐ qù diàoyú.
example.english: He went fishing with his father.
example.fact: 父 is a formal and written 'father': 父亲 is the formal term and 爸爸 the everyday one. It builds 父母 (parents) and 祖父 (paternal grandfather). 父 can also be read fǔ in a few old terms of respect for men.

examples.hanzi: 父亲节我给爸爸做了一顿饭。
examples.pinyin: Fùqīnjié wǒ gěi bàba zuò le yí dùn fàn.
examples.english: On Father's Day I cooked a meal for Dad.

examples.hanzi: 这位老人是我的祖父。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎorén shì wǒ de zǔfù.
examples.english: This elderly man is my grandfather.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 职 is the duty one hears and remembers.
只 (zhī) is a near sound match for zhí; also in 织 zhī and 识 shí.

example.hanzi: 他的职业是医生。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhíyè shì yīshēng.
example.english: His profession is a doctor.
example.fact: 职 appears in job words: 职业 (profession), 职位 (position), 职员 (staff), 辞职 (to resign), 升职 (to be promoted), 职责 (duty). It does not usually stand alone.

examples.hanzi: 我想申请这个职位。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng shēnqǐng zhège zhíwèi.
examples.english: I'd like to apply for this position.

examples.hanzi: 他在公司担任重要职务。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī dānrèn zhòngyào zhíwù.
examples.english: He holds an important post in the company.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — boundaries and surroundings: 国 country, 园 garden, 回 return; 图 is a drawn plan of a region.
书 (simplified 書) — the old form shows a brush 聿 writing; to write, then what is written: book, letter.
饣 (food, simplified 食) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱; 馆 is an inn or restaurant, a place that serves food.
官 (guān) sounds exactly like 馆 apart from tone; also in 管 guǎn.

example.hanzi: 我每天下午去图书馆看书。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān xiàwǔ qù túshūguǎn kàn shū.
example.english: I go to the library every afternoon to read.
example.fact: 图书馆 is almost perfectly transparent — 图 ("picture/chart") + 书 ("book") + 馆 ("hall") literally spell out "picture-and-book hall" — a modern compound coined to name the Western-style public library, distinct from older native terms like 藏书楼 ("book-storage tower") for a private book collection.

examples.hanzi: 这个图书馆星期天也开门。
examples.pinyin: Zhège túshūguǎn xīngqītiān yě kāimén.
examples.english: This library is open on Sundays too.

examples.hanzi: 我在图书馆借了三本书。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài túshūguǎn jiè le sān běn shū.
examples.english: I borrowed three books at the library.

components.note: 日 (sun) — light and brightness: 明, 晴, 时; 显 is something lit up and clear to see.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 她今天显得特别开心。
example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān xiǎnde tèbié kāixīn.
example.english: She seems especially happy today.
example.fact: 显得 must be followed by an adjective describing how something comes across (显得 + adj.), the same way English "seems" works — it can't take a noun object directly, so "seems like an expert" needs the extra word 像 (显得像专家), not a bare noun after 显得.

examples.hanzi: 他看起来很累，显得比实际年龄老。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlái hěn lèi, xiǎnde bǐ shíjì niánlíng lǎo.
examples.english: He looks tired and seems older than his real age.

examples.hanzi: 穿上这件衣服，你显得更高了。
examples.pinyin: Chuān shàng zhè jiàn yīfu, nǐ xiǎnde gèng gāo le.
examples.english: In this outfit, you look taller.

components.note: 歹 (bad bone) — death and decay, as in 残 remnant, 烈 fierce, 殊 special.
匕 (person) — a person beside bones: death.
刂 (knife) — marks cutting and punishing, as in 别, 刻, 划; 刑 is a punishment.
开 (a worn-down 幵) gives the sound exactly: 刑 xíng, also in 形 xíng and 型 xíng.

example.hanzi: 那名罪犯被判处死刑。
example.pinyin: Nà míng zuìfàn bèi pànchǔ sǐxíng.
example.english: That criminal was sentenced to the death penalty.
example.fact: 死刑's two characters need no unpacking — 死 ("to die") plus 刑 ("punishment," itself pairing bars 开 with a knife 刂) name the death penalty as literally as English does, sitting at the most severe end of China's ladder of criminal penalties (刑罚).

examples.hanzi: 法院判处这名罪犯死刑。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn pànchǔ zhè míng zuìfàn sǐxíng.
examples.english: The court sentenced the criminal to death.

examples.hanzi: 有些国家已经取消了死刑。
examples.pinyin: Yǒuxiē guójiā yǐjīng qǔxiāo le sǐxíng.
examples.english: Some countries have already abolished the death penalty.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说, 话, 请; 谎 is a spoken lie.
荒 (huāng) sounds the same as 谎 huǎng except for tone; also 慌 huāng.

example.hanzi: 他对我说谎了。
example.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ shuō huǎng le.
example.english: He lied to me.
example.fact: 谎 is a lie: 说谎 (tell a lie), 撒谎 (tell lies), 谎话 (lie), 谎言 (falsehood). 善意的谎言 is a white lie.

examples.hanzi: 他对老师撒了一个谎。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì lǎoshī sā le yí ge huǎng.
examples.english: He told the teacher a lie.

examples.hanzi: 小孩子不要说谎话。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoháizi bú yào shuō huǎnghuà.
examples.english: Kids shouldn't tell lies.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
止 (foot) — two footprints, one above the other, make a step; the same 止 is in 走 walk and 跑 run.

example.hanzi: 你的中文进步很快。
example.pinyin: Nǐ de Zhōngwén jìnbù hěn kuài.
example.english: Your Chinese is progressing very quickly.
example.fact: 进步 works as both a verb ("to improve," 他进步了 "he's improved") and a noun/adjective ("progress; progressive," as in 进步人士 "progressive people") — one word doing the job that English splits across "progress," "improve," and "progressive."

examples.hanzi: 他的成绩比上学期进步了很多。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì bǐ shàng xuéqī jìnbù le hěn duō.
examples.english: His grades improved a lot compared with last semester.

examples.hanzi: 科学技术的进步改变了我们的生活。
examples.pinyin: Kēxué jìshù de jìnbù gǎibiàn le wǒmen de shēnghuó.
examples.english: Advances in science and technology have changed our lives.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — the "walk/road" radical appears in characters of going and moving — 过, 进, 送, 逃; here it shows running after something.
求 (seek) — the original picture of a fur coat (裘 qiú adds 衣); "seek, request" is a borrowed use. 求 sounds out 球 qiú and 救 jiù.

example.hanzi: 他一直在追求自己的音乐梦想。
example.pinyin: Tā yìzhí zài zhuīqiú zìjǐ de yīnyuè mèngxiǎng.
example.english: He has always been pursuing his dream of music.
example.fact: 追求 covers chasing an abstract goal (追求梦想, "to pursue a dream") and romantically courting a person (追求她, "to woo her") with the same verb — Chinese leans on this word for courtship more heavily than English speakers might expect from "pursue" alone.

examples.hanzi: 很多年轻人在追求自由的生活。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō niánqīng rén zài zhuīqiú zìyóu de shēnghuó.
examples.english: Many young people are pursuing a free lifestyle.

examples.hanzi: 他追求了她三年，她才答应。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhuīqiú le tā sān nián, tā cái dāying.
examples.english: He pursued her for three years before she said yes.

components.note: 友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.
⺈ (bent figure) — the top part of 尔, a variant stroke group. 尔 is an old form of 'you'; today it appears mainly in foreign names like 比尔 Bill.
小 (small) — the bottom part and radical, as in 少 few. The shape does not explain 'you'; the character is now mostly sound-borrowed.
兰 (orchid) — simplified from 蘭, which had the grass radical 艹 on top and 闌 giving the sound lán — a plant name.

example.hanzi: 他的祖父母来自爱尔兰。
example.pinyin: Tā de zǔfùmǔ láizì Ài'ěrlán.
example.english: His grandparents are from Ireland.
example.fact: 爱尔兰 is a sound-only transliteration of "Ireland" — 爱 ("love") and 兰 ("orchid") contribute nothing to the meaning here, but they're conventionally pleasant characters that Chinese reserves for rendering foreign place names it wants to sound agreeable, unlike some more neutral characters used for less favored names historically.

examples.hanzi: 爱尔兰的草地一年四季都是绿的。
examples.pinyin: Ài'ěrlán de cǎodì yì nián sìjì dōu shì lǜ de.
examples.english: Ireland's grass is green all year round.

examples.hanzi: 我去爱尔兰旅游的时候，吃了很多土豆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù Ài'ěrlán lǚyóu de shíhou, chī le hěn duō tǔdòu.
examples.english: When I traveled to Ireland, I ate a lot of potatoes.

components.note: 亨 (hēng) — mainly seen in names like 亨利; as a part it sounds out 哼 hēng and 烹 pēng.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.hanzi: 亨利是我们班唯一的外国学生。
example.pinyin: Hēnglì shì wǒmen bān wéiyī de wàiguó xuésheng.
example.english: Henry is the only foreign student in our class.
example.fact: 亨利 is a pure sound transliteration of "Henry" — 亨 (hēng) independently means "smooth, prosperous" (as in the Book of Changes) but contributes nothing to the name here. The same two characters, written in lowercase as "henry," also happen to name the SI unit of electrical inductance, honoring physicist Joseph Henry.

examples.hanzi: 亨利每天晚上都在练习中文。
examples.pinyin: Hēnglì měi tiān wǎnshang dōu zài liànxí Zhōngwén.
examples.english: Henry practices Chinese every evening.

examples.hanzi: 你见过亨利的妹妹吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiàn guo Hēnglì de mèimei ma?
examples.english: Have you met Henry's younger sister?

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and plants, as in 花 flower, 草 grass, 茶 tea; 苹 is the apple (苹果).
平 (píng) gives the sound exactly: 苹 píng, also in 评 píng.
木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.hanzi: 我每天早上吃一个苹果。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang chī yí gè píngguǒ.
example.english: I eat an apple every morning.
example.fact: 苹 exists mainly to write this one word — it pairs the plant radical 艹 with the phonetic 平 (píng) purely for sound, carrying no independent meaning outside 苹果, a common pattern for characters coined specifically to name a fruit or other borrowed thing.

examples.hanzi: 我想买两斤苹果。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi liǎng jīn píngguǒ.
examples.english: I'd like to buy two jin of apples.

examples.hanzi: 苹果树上结满了红红的苹果。
examples.pinyin: Píngguǒ shù shang jiē mǎn le hónghóng de píngguǒ.
examples.english: The apple tree is full of red apples.

components.note: 南 (nán) — south; as a part it sounds out 楠 nán and 喃 nán.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 冬天,他喜欢去南方过冬。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān, tā xǐhuan qù nánfāng guòdōng.
example.english: In winter, he likes to go south to spend the winter.
example.fact: 南, like the other cardinal-direction characters 东西北, has an ancient pictographic origin unrelated to direction — it's thought to have first depicted a hanging bell or musical instrument, its shape simply borrowed later to write the unrelated word "south."

examples.hanzi: 南方的冬天不太冷。
examples.pinyin: Nánfāng de dōngtiān bú tài lěng.
examples.english: Winters in the south are not very cold.

examples.hanzi: 他是南方人，喜欢吃米饭。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì nánfāng rén, xǐhuan chī mǐfàn.
examples.english: He is from the south and likes eating rice.

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 她天生就有一副好嗓子。
example.pinyin: Tā tiānshēng jiù yǒu yí fù hǎo sǎngzi.
example.english: She was born with a wonderful voice.
example.fact: 天生 literally means "born of heaven" (天 "sky/heaven" + 生 "to be born"), reflecting an older worldview that treated innate talent as a gift bestowed from above — much like the English idiom "a natural," which also frames unlearned ability as something given rather than earned.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子天生就爱唱歌。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi tiānshēng jiù ài chàng gē.
examples.english: This child loves singing by nature.

examples.hanzi: 他天生聪明，学什么都很快。
examples.pinyin: Tā tiānshēng cōngmíng, xué shénme dōu hěn kuài.
examples.english: He is naturally smart and learns everything fast.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 傻 is a foolish person.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 别把我当傻子。
example.pinyin: Bié bǎ wǒ dàng shǎzi.
example.english: Don't treat me like a fool.
example.fact: 傻 combines 亻 ("person") with an element depicting a blow to the crown of the head (囟) — a blunt visual joke suggesting someone whose wits have been knocked loose, the likely picture behind its meaning "foolish, stupid."

examples.hanzi: 我可不是傻子，这种话我才不信。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kě bú shì shǎzi, zhè zhǒng huà wǒ cái bú xìn.
examples.english: I'm no fool; I won't believe that kind of talk.

examples.hanzi: 他假装做傻子，其实什么都明白。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎzhuāng zuò shǎzi, qíshí shénme dōu míngbai.
examples.english: He pretends to be a fool, but actually understands everything.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and washing, as in 洗 wash, 游 swim, 洗澡; 浴 is a bath.
谷 (yù/gǔ) gives the sound: 浴 yù, also in 欲 yù and 裕 yù.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 浴室里的热水器坏了。
example.pinyin: Yùshì lǐ de rèshuǐqì huài le.
example.english: The water heater in the bathroom is broken.
example.fact: 浴室 names the room by function — 浴 ("to bathe") + 室 ("room") — and in everyday Mainland usage leans toward a dedicated bathing/shower room, while the more common word for a full bathroom including the toilet is 卫生间 ("hygiene room"), a distinction English's single word "bathroom" doesn't force speakers to make.

examples.hanzi: 我正在浴室里洗澡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhèngzài yùshì lǐ xǐzǎo.
examples.english: I'm taking a bath in the bathroom.

examples.hanzi: 浴室的地板很滑，要小心。
examples.pinyin: Yùshì de dìbǎn hěn huá, yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: The bathroom floor is slippery, so be careful.

components.note: 求 (seek) — the original picture of a fur coat (裘 qiú adds 衣); "seek, request" is a borrowed use. 求 sounds out 球 qiú and 救 jiù.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 他在海边向她求婚了。
example.pinyin: Tā zài hǎibiān xiàng tā qiúhūn le.
example.english: He proposed to her on the beach.
example.fact: 求婚 usually takes its target with the coverb 向 (向她求婚, "to propose to her") rather than as a bare direct object — learners transferring the English pattern "propose to her" often try 求婚她 by mistake, which sounds off to native ears.

examples.hanzi: 他准备了戒指，打算向她求婚。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǔnbèi le jièzhi, dǎsuàn xiàng tā qiúhūn.
examples.english: He prepared a ring and plans to propose to her.

examples.hanzi: 她答应了他的求婚。
examples.pinyin: Tā dāying le tā de qiúhūn.
examples.english: She accepted his marriage proposal.

meanings: short stories of the Tang and Song Dynasty

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
奇 (qí) is a sound clue for 骑 qí, 寄 jì, 椅 yǐ and 崎 qí; as a word it means strange or remarkable.

example.hanzi: 他的一生充满传奇色彩。
example.pinyin: Tā de yìshēng chōngmǎn chuánqí sècǎi.
example.english: His life was filled with a legendary quality.
example.fact: 传奇 began as the specific name for a genre of marvel tales and dramatic romances from the Tang and Song dynasties before its modern sense of "legendary, larger-than-life" grew out of that literary label — much as English "epic" widened from a specific poetic genre into a casual adjective.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个关于英雄的传奇故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge guānyú yīngxióng de chuánqí gùshi.
examples.english: This is a legendary story about a hero.

examples.hanzi: 这位老人的经历很传奇。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎorén de jīnglì hěn chuánqí.
examples.english: This old man's life story is quite legendary.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wooden things, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; 杆 is a pole or shaft.
干 (gān) — same sound: 杆 gān. 干 also sounds out 肝 gān and 赶 gǎn.

example.hanzi: 旗杆上挂着一面红旗。
example.pinyin: Qígān shàng guà zhe yí miàn hóngqí.
example.english: A red flag is hanging on the flagpole.
example.fact: 杆 is a long pole: 旗杆 (flagpole), 电线杆 (utility pole), 钓鱼杆 (fishing rod). Read gǎn, it is a barrel or stalk, as in 笔杆 (pen barrel) and a measure word for rifles (一杆枪).

examples.hanzi: 路边立着一根电线杆。
examples.pinyin: Lù biān lì zhe yì gēn diànxiàn gān.
examples.english: A utility pole stands by the roadside.

examples.hanzi: 他用杆子把苹果打了下来。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng gānzi bǎ píngguǒ dǎ le xiàlái.
examples.english: He knocked the apples down with a pole.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and herbs: 花 flower, 草 grass, 茶 tea; 苦 first named a bitter herb.
古 (gǔ) is a loose clue for kǔ — see also 枯 kū and 姑 gū.

example.hanzi: 这个药很苦。
example.pinyin: Zhège yào hěn kǔ.
example.english: This medicine is very bitter.
example.fact: 苦 is bitter, but also hardship: 吃苦 ('eat bitterness') means to endure hardship. 辛苦 is 'hard work', and 辛苦了 is how you thank someone for their effort. 苦瓜 is bitter melon.

examples.hanzi: 这杯咖啡太苦了,我要加糖。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi kāfēi tài kǔ le, wǒ yào jiā táng.
examples.english: This coffee is too bitter; I'll add sugar.

examples.hanzi: 他从小吃了很多苦。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo chī le hěn duō kǔ.
examples.english: He suffered a lot of hardship since childhood.

components.note: 斗 (dipper, measure) — measuring grain and liquids: 科, 斜, 升; 料 is rice 米 measured out, then material.

example.hanzi: 请把材料准备好。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ cáiliào zhǔnbèi hǎo.
example.english: Please get the materials ready.
example.fact: 料 means raw material and stuff: 材料 (material), 饮料 (drink), 资料 (data), 调料 (seasoning), 料理 (cuisine, as in 日本料理). It can also mean 'to expect': 出乎意料 is 'beyond expectation'.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜用了很多调料。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài yòng le hěn duō tiáoliào.
examples.english: This dish uses a lot of seasonings.

examples.hanzi: 你来了,真是出乎意料。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lái le, zhēn shì chūhū yìliào.
examples.english: You came; what a surprise.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wooden things, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; 枚 was a tree stalk; now it is a measure word for small items like coins and stamps.

example.hanzi: 他得到了一枚金牌。
example.pinyin: Tā dédào le yì méi jīnpái.
example.english: He won a gold medal.
example.fact: 枚 is a formal measure word for small, flat or compact items: 一枚硬币 (a coin), 一枚戒指 (a ring), 一枚奖牌 (a medal), 一枚导弹 (a missile). The idiom 不胜枚举 means 'too many to list one by one'.

examples.hanzi: 他的口袋里有一枚硬币。
examples.pinyin: Tā de kǒudài li yǒu yì méi yìngbì.
examples.english: There is a coin in his pocket.

examples.hanzi: 这枚邮票很珍贵。
examples.pinyin: Zhè méi yóupiào hěn zhēnguì.
examples.english: This stamp is very valuable.

meanings: sentence-final particle for a cheerful announcement

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 喽 is a particle added to sentence ends.
娄 (lóu) — same sound: 喽 lóu. 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu and 屡 lǚ.

example.hanzi: 开饭喽!
example.pinyin: Kāifàn lou!
example.english: Dinner's ready!
example.fact: 喽 is a lively sentence-final particle, roughly a blend of 了 and 哦, used to announce something: 走喽 (off we go). It is also read lóu in 喽啰 (minions, henchmen in a bandit gang), where 喽 has its own history.

examples.hanzi: 好喽,我们出发喽!
examples.pinyin: Hǎo lou, wǒmen chūfā lou!
examples.english: All right, off we go!

examples.hanzi: 放假喽,大家都很开心。
examples.pinyin: Fàngjià lou, dàjiā dōu hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: Holiday time! Everyone is happy.

components.note: 石 (stone) — a rock 口 at the foot of a cliff 厂; as a radical it marks stones and minerals, as in 破, 码, 砖, 磨.

example.hanzi: 河边有很多大石头。
example.pinyin: Hébiān yǒu hěn duō dà shítou.
example.english: There are lots of big rocks by the river.
example.fact: 石 is stone: 石头 (stone), 石油 (petroleum, 'rock oil'), 钻石 (diamond), 化石 (fossil). Read dàn, 石 was an old unit of grain, about 100 liters; 石 is also a surname.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在海边捡小石子。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài hǎibiān jiǎn xiǎo shízǐ.
examples.english: The kids are picking up pebbles by the sea.

examples.hanzi: 这是一块很漂亮的宝石。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí kuài hěn piàoliang de bǎoshí.
examples.english: This is a very beautiful gemstone.

components.note: 会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.hanzi: 两国领导人今天举行了会见。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó lǐngdǎorén jīntiān jǔxíngle huìjiàn.
example.english: The leaders of the two countries held a meeting today.
example.fact: 会见 sits at the formal, diplomatic end of Chinese's "to meet" vocabulary, reserved for official meetings between officials or dignitaries — everyday meetings with friends instead use 见面 or the bare verb 见, a register distinction English's single verb "to meet" doesn't mark.

examples.hanzi: 总统明天将会见来访的客人。
examples.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng míngtiān jiāng huìjiàn lái fǎng de kèrén.
examples.english: The president will meet visiting guests tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 记者会见了获奖的科学家。
examples.pinyin: Jìzhě huìjiàn le huòjiǎng de kēxuéjiā.
examples.english: The reporter met with the award-winning scientist.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.

example.hanzi: 医生建议他每天走路半小时。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā měitiān zǒulù bàn xiǎoshí.
example.english: The doctor recommended he walk for half an hour every day.
example.fact: 走路 specifically emphasizes moving under one's own two feet — its bare root 走, by contrast, more often just means "to leave" or "to go" in everyday speech (我先走了, "I'm heading out now"), a meaning drift away from its ancient sense of brisk walking or running.

examples.hanzi: 从家到学校，走路要二十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Cóng jiā dào xuéxiào, zǒulù yào èrshí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: From home to school, it takes twenty minutes on foot.

examples.hanzi: 小宝宝已经会走路了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo bǎobao yǐjīng huì zǒulù le.
examples.english: The baby can already walk.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 主动权掌握在我们手中。
example.pinyin: Zhǔdòngquán zhǎngwò zài wǒmen shǒuzhōng.
example.english: The initiative is in our hands.
example.fact: 手中 joins the concrete 手 ("hand") with 中 ("within, in the middle of") to mean not just "physically in the hand" but, by extension, "within someone's control or possession" — the same literal-to-figurative shift English makes with "in someone's hands."

examples.hanzi: 他手中拿着一本旧书。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǒuzhōng ná zhe yì běn jiù shū.
examples.english: He held an old book in his hand.

examples.hanzi: 这笔钱现在不在我手中。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ qián xiànzài bú zài wǒ shǒuzhōng.
examples.english: I don't have this money on me right now.

components.note: 心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.hanzi: 从他的表情可以想见他有多失望。
example.pinyin: Cóng tā de biǎoqíng kěyǐ xiǎngjiàn tā yǒu duō shīwàng.
example.english: From his expression, one can well imagine how disappointed he is.
example.fact: 想见 isn't "to think about seeing someone," as its parts 想 ("to think") and 见 ("to see") might suggest to a beginner — it actually means "to infer, to vividly imagine," and almost always follows 可以 or 不难 ("可以想见," "不难想见") to introduce a conclusion drawn from indirect evidence.

examples.hanzi: 看到他那么高兴，可以想见比赛赢得多不容易。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào tā nàme gāoxìng, kěyǐ xiǎngjiàn bǐsài yíng de duō bù róngyì.
examples.english: Seeing how happy he was, you can imagine how hard the game was to win.

examples.hanzi: 从这封信里，可以想见他当时的心情。
examples.pinyin: Cóng zhè fēng xìn lǐ, kěyǐ xiǎngjiàn tā dāngshí de xīnqíng.
examples.english: From this letter, you can imagine how he felt at the time.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks liquids, as in 河, 汤, 油; 涂 is to smear on liquid or paint.
余 (yú) is a loose hint for tú; 途 tú shares it.

example.hanzi: 他在墙上涂了一层漆。
example.pinyin: Tā zài qiáng shàng tú le yì céng qī.
example.english: He applied a coat of paint to the wall.
example.fact: 涂 is to spread something on a surface: 涂药 (apply ointment), 涂改 (to alter by erasing), 涂鸦 (graffiti, 'smeared crows'). 糊涂 means confused or muddled.

examples.hanzi: 他在面包上涂了一层果酱。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài miànbāo shang tú le yì céng guǒjiàng.
examples.english: He spread a layer of jam on the bread.

examples.hanzi: 请在伤口上涂一点药。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài shāngkǒu shang tú yìdiǎn yào.
examples.english: Please put a little medicine on the wound.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你, 他, 们; 伊 is a literary she/he and a name syllable.
尹 (yǐn) is only a loose sound hint for yī.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.hanzi: 那位记者常年在伊拉克报道战争新闻。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi jìzhě chángnián zài Yīlākè bàodào zhànzhēng xīnwén.
example.english: That reporter has reported war news from Iraq for years.
example.fact: 伊拉克 is a sound-only transliteration of "Iraq" — 伊 (a formal third-person pronoun in Classical Chinese), 拉 ("to pull"), and 克 ("gram; to overcome") are chosen purely for their pronunciation, with no attempt at meaning, typical of how Chinese renders country names with no older Chinese-coined equivalent.

examples.hanzi: 伊拉克的夏天非常热。
examples.pinyin: Yīlākè de xiàtiān fēicháng rè.
examples.english: Summers in Iraq are extremely hot.

examples.hanzi: 这位作家曾经在伊拉克住过两年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā céngjīng zài Yīlākè zhù guo liǎng nián.
examples.english: This writer once lived in Iraq for two years.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.hanzi: 这本书我已经看了不止三次。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū wǒ yǐjīng kànle bùzhǐ sān cì.
example.english: I've already read this book more than three times.
example.fact: 不止 is easy to confuse with the near-homophone 不只 — 不止 (built on 止, "to stop") literally means "doesn't stop at," giving its sense of "more than, exceeding," while 不只 pairs with 而且 to mean "not only... but also"; mixing up the two characters is a common slip even among native speakers.

examples.hanzi: 他的咳嗽不止一天了，应该去看医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā de késou bùzhǐ yì tiān le, yīnggāi qù kàn yīshēng.
examples.english: His cough has lasted more than a day; he should see a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 他笑得不止，肚子都疼了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiào de bùzhǐ, dùzi dōu téng le.
examples.english: He laughed so much that his stomach hurt.

components.note: 页 (head) — heads and faces, as in 头, 题, 顶: to turn the head and look.
厄 stands in for 雇 (gù) in the traditional 顧; the clue is only loose today.
门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.

example.hanzi: 他退休后担任公司的顾问。
example.pinyin: Tā tuìxiū hòu dānrèn gōngsī de gùwèn.
example.english: After retiring, he serves as the company's adviser.
example.fact: 顾问 combines 顾 ("to look back at, to consider," from 页 "head" — turning one's head to look) with 问 ("to ask") — literally "one you look to and ask," a fairly transparent image for someone whose job is to be consulted.

examples.hanzi: 公司请他当技术顾问。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī qǐng tā dāng jìshù gùwèn.
examples.english: The company asked him to be a technical consultant.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要一位法律顾问来帮忙。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào yí wèi fǎlǜ gùwèn lái bāngmáng.
examples.english: We need a legal adviser to help.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) on the left — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 陆, 附, 阶; 障 is a barrier.
章 (zhāng) hints at the sound: 障 zhàng is close, as in 彰 zhāng.
石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破 break, 码, 砖 brick; a stone in the road is an obstacle.

example.hanzi: 语言是他们交流的最大障碍。
example.pinyin: Yǔyán shì tāmen jiāoliú de zuìdà zhàng'ài.
example.english: Language is the biggest obstacle to their communication.
example.fact: Both halves of 障碍 independently mean "to block" — 障 (mound/wall radical 阝) and 碍 (stone radical 石) — a doubled-synonym compound built the same way as 喜欢 and 应该 from the pilot batch, where two near-synonymous characters reinforce a single meaning.

examples.hanzi: 害羞是他交朋友的障碍。
examples.pinyin: Hàixiū shì tā jiāo péngyou de zhàng'ài.
examples.english: Being shy is a hindrance to his making friends.

examples.hanzi: 路上有障碍，车子过不去。
examples.pinyin: Lù shang yǒu zhàng'ài, chēzi guò bú qù.
examples.english: There is an obstacle on the road and the car can't get through.

components.note: 危 (danger) — a person at the top of a cliff, with another person kneeling below: a precarious spot.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 这家公司正面临严重的财务危机。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhèng miànlín yánzhòng de cáiwù wēijī.
example.english: This company is currently facing a serious financial crisis.
example.fact: 危机 combines 危 ("danger," from a pictograph of someone crouched at a cliff's edge) with 机 ("mechanism; pivotal juncture") — the basis for the popular claim that Chinese "crisis" is built from "danger" plus "opportunity." The etymology of the two characters is real, but many linguists caution that 机 here means something closer to "a critical turning point" than "a chance to profit."

examples.hanzi: 这场危机让很多人失去了工作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng wēijī ràng hěn duō rén shīqù le gōngzuò.
examples.english: This crisis made many people lose their jobs.

examples.hanzi: 在危机面前，他保持着冷静。
examples.pinyin: Zài wēijī miànqián, tā bǎochí zhe lěngjìng.
examples.english: In the face of the crisis, he stayed calm.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — marks action and effort, as in 数, 教, 放, 改; 敏 is quick and sharp.
每 (měi) hints at the sound: 敏 mǐn is close.
心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 这个话题在办公室里很敏感。
example.pinyin: Zhège huàtí zài bàngōngshì lǐ hěn mǐngǎn.
example.english: This topic is very sensitive in the office.
example.fact: 敏感 covers both physical sensitivity (皮肤敏感, "sensitive skin") and social sensitivity (敏感话题, "a sensitive topic"), paralleling English "sensitive" — but 敏 alone already means "quick, sharp-witted," so the word leans toward "quick to perceive or react" rather than "easily hurt."

examples.hanzi: 她的皮肤很敏感，不能用这种面霜。
examples.pinyin: Tā de pífū hěn mǐngǎn, bù néng yòng zhè zhǒng miànshuāng.
examples.english: Her skin is sensitive and she can't use this kind of face cream.

examples.hanzi: 他对别人的评价非常敏感。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì biéren de píngjià fēicháng mǐngǎn.
examples.english: He is very sensitive to what others say about him.

components.note: 走 (walk) — marks walking and going, as in 起 rise, 赶 hurry; 趁 is going while the chance lasts, as in 趁热 while hot.

example.hanzi: 趁热吃吧。
example.pinyin: Chèn rè chī ba.
example.english: Eat it while it's hot.
example.fact: 趁 means to take advantage of a moment: 趁热 (while hot), 趁早 (as early as possible), 趁机 (seize the opportunity), 趁年轻 (while young). 趁火打劫 is 'to rob a house on fire', that is, to profit from someone's trouble.

examples.hanzi: 趁天气好,我们去爬山吧。
examples.pinyin: Chèn tiānqì hǎo, wǒmen qù páshān ba.
examples.english: While the weather is nice, let's go hiking.

examples.hanzi: 你趁早去医院看看吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ chèn zǎo qù yīyuàn kànkan ba.
examples.english: You'd better go see a doctor early.

components.note: 十 (ten) — complete and wide: 博 is broad, abundant.
尃 (fū) is a loose sound clue for bó; 尃 also in 搏 bó, 薄 báo and 缚 fù.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.
饣 (food, simplified 食) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱; 馆 is an inn or restaurant, a place that serves food.
官 (guān) sounds exactly like 馆 apart from tone; also in 管 guǎn.

example.hanzi: 周末我们打算去博物馆看展览。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen dǎsuàn qù bówùguǎn kàn zhǎnlǎn.
example.english: This weekend we plan to go to the museum to see an exhibition.
example.fact: 博物馆 — literally "hall (馆) of broad (博) things (物)" — is a late-19th/early-20th-century coinage modeled on the Western museum, and is often grouped with words like 经济 and 社会 as one of many modern institutional terms that Chinese picked up via Japanese kanji compounds coined during the Meiji era.

examples.hanzi: 这家博物馆里有很多古代的文物。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā bówùguǎn lǐ yǒu hěn duō gǔdài de wénwù.
examples.english: This museum has many ancient artifacts.

examples.hanzi: 博物馆星期一不开门。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn xīngqīyī bù kāimén.
examples.english: The museum is closed on Mondays.

components.note: 周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.
二 (two) — the top and bottom bars. Dictionary story: five elements between heaven and earth, with a cross in the middle; memory aid, not firmly attested.

example.hanzi: 我们周五晚上有聚会。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōuwǔ wǎnshang yǒu jùhuì.
example.english: We have a get-together on Friday evening.
example.fact: 周五 numbers the weekdays starting from Monday as "one" (周一 Monday ... 周五 Friday), with 周日 or 星期天 set aside for Sunday — a plain numbered system that contrasts with English weekday names rooted in old gods and celestial bodies (Saturn's day, Moon's day, and so on).

examples.hanzi: 周五下午我们要开一个会。
examples.pinyin: Zhōuwǔ xiàwǔ wǒmen yào kāi yí ge huì.
examples.english: We have a meeting on Friday afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 你周五有空吗？一起吃饭吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhōuwǔ yǒu kòng ma? Yìqǐ chī fàn ba.
examples.english: Are you free on Friday? Let's have a meal together.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摄 is taking hold, then capturing on camera, as in 拍摄.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 像 is a person's likeness.
象 (xiàng, elephant) gives the exact sound; 象 first meant elephant, then "image".
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 婚礼现场架着好几台摄像机。
example.pinyin: Hūnlǐ xiànchǎng jiàzhe hǎojǐ tái shèxiàngjī.
example.english: Several video cameras were set up at the wedding venue.
example.fact: 摄像机 (a video/movie camera) and 照相机 (a still camera) share no character besides the generic 机 ("machine") — 摄 means "to capture, take in" while 照 means "to shine light on, illuminate," a lexical line between capturing motion and capturing a lit still image that English's single word "camera" blurs together.

examples.hanzi: 他买了一台新的摄像机来拍旅行视频。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi le yì tái xīn de shèxiàngjī lái pāi lǚxíng shìpín.
examples.english: He bought a new video camera to shoot travel videos.

examples.hanzi: 摄像机正对着舞台中央。
examples.pinyin: Shèxiàngjī zhèng duì zhe wǔtái zhōngyāng.
examples.english: The video camera is pointed at the center of the stage.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.

example.hanzi: 他失去了工作。
example.pinyin: Tā shīqù le gōngzuò.
example.english: He lost his job.
example.fact: 失 is a more formal and abstract 'lose': 失去 (to lose), 失败 (to fail), 失望 (disappointed), 失业 (unemployed), 失眠 (insomnia). For misplacing objects, speakers say 丢 (diū).

examples.hanzi: 这次比赛他们失败了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài tāmen shībài le.
examples.english: They lost this match.

examples.hanzi: 对不起,我失约了。
examples.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ shīyuē le.
examples.english: Sorry, I broke my promise.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
石 (stone) — stones and hard things: 研, 码, 砖; 破 is to smash or break.
皮 (pí) is a loose sound clue; same series 坡 pō, 披 pī, 波 bō.

example.hanzi: 他打破了世界纪录。
example.pinyin: Tā dǎpòle shìjiè jìlù.
example.english: He broke the world record.
example.fact: Beyond physically shattering an object, 打破 extends metaphorically to breaking records (打破纪录), breaking silence (打破沉默), and breaking old habits or conventions (打破常规) — much like English "break" spans the same range from literal smashing to abstract disruption.

examples.hanzi: 不小心，我把杯子打破了。
examples.pinyin: Bù xiǎoxīn, wǒ bǎ bēizi dǎpò le.
examples.english: I accidentally broke the cup.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌打破了当年的销售纪录。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē dǎpò le dāngnián de xiāoshòu jìlù.
examples.english: This song broke the sales record that year.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 他手下有二十几名员工。
example.pinyin: Tā shǒuxià yǒu èrshí jǐ míng yuángōng.
example.english: He has more than twenty employees under him.
example.fact: 手下 literally means "under the hand" (手 "hand" + 下 "below") and can name one's subordinates (他的手下, "his men") or describe the moment of taking action, as in the idiom 手下留情 — literally "leave mercy under the hand" — meaning "go easy on someone."

examples.hanzi: 这位经理手下的员工都很努力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi jīnglǐ shǒuxià de yuángōng dōu hěn nǔlì.
examples.english: The employees under this manager all work hard.

examples.hanzi: 我手下现在没有那么多钱。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shǒuxià xiànzài méiyǒu nàme duō qián.
examples.english: I don't have that much money on hand right now.

components.note: 文 (writing, culture) — a person with a patterned chest, early tattooed designs, which became writing and culture. Also in 纹 wén and 蚊 wén.
化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.

example.hanzi: 每个国家都有自己独特的文化。
example.pinyin: Měi gè guójiā dōu yǒu zìjǐ dútè de wénhuà.
example.english: Every country has its own unique culture.
example.fact: 文化 literally means "the transformation (化) brought about by pattern/writing (文)" — 文 originally pictured decorative markings or tattoos on a chest before broadening to mean "writing, civility, culture." The compound was popularized in its modern sense partly through early-20th-century translations of the Western concept of "culture."

examples.hanzi: 我想了解中国的饮食文化。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng liǎojiě Zhōngguó de yǐnshí wénhuà.
examples.english: I want to learn about Chinese food culture.

examples.hanzi: 他很有文化，读了很多书。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn yǒu wénhuà, dú le hěn duō shū.
examples.english: He is well educated and has read many books.

components.note: 马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.hanzi: 马克是我在德国认识的第一个朋友。
example.pinyin: Mǎkè shì wǒ zài Déguó rènshi de dì yī gè péngyou.
example.english: Mark was the first friend I made in Germany.
example.fact: 马克 does double duty as both the transliterated name "Mark" and the old German currency "(Deutsche) Mark" — the same two characters, chosen purely for their sound, happen to cover two unrelated foreign words, a common outcome when Chinese borrows short foreign terms phonetically.

examples.hanzi: 我和马克在同一家公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé Mǎkè zài tóng yì jiā gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.english: Mark and I work at the same company.

examples.hanzi: 马克下个月要搬到北京。
examples.pinyin: Mǎkè xià ge yuè yào bān dào Běijīng.
examples.english: Mark is moving to Beijing next month.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and roads, as in 过, 进, 送; 遵 is to follow a path.
尊 (zūn) gives the sound exactly: 遵 zūn, and also gives the sense of honouring.
宀 (roof) — a house or shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; a hand 寸 under a roof means guarding.
寸 (hand, inch) — originally a hand, as in 对, 寻, 封.

example.hanzi: 每个员工都应该遵守公司的规定。
example.pinyin: Měi gè yuángōng dōu yīnggāi zūnshǒu gōngsī de guīdìng.
example.english: Every employee should abide by the company's rules.
example.fact: 遵守 pairs 遵 ("to follow respectfully," 辶 "to walk" + 尊 "to honor") with 守 ("to guard, keep to") for the everyday word for obeying rules or laws; its more formal cousin 遵循 swaps in 循 ("to follow a path") for a slightly more written, bookish register.

examples.hanzi: 请大家遵守交通规则。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā zūnshǒu jiāotōng guīzé.
examples.english: Everyone, please follow the traffic rules.

examples.hanzi: 我们必须遵守法律。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū zūnshǒu fǎlǜ.
examples.english: We must abide by the law.

components.note: 飞 (fly) — simplified from 飛, a bird with spread wings.
舟 (boat) — 舟 is the boat radical, as in 般, 航, 舰; 船 is a ship.

example.hanzi: 神舟飞船成功返回地球。
example.pinyin: Shénzhōu fēichuán chénggōng fǎnhuí dìqiú.
example.english: The Shenzhou spacecraft successfully returned to Earth.
example.fact: 飞船 literally means "flying boat" (飞 "to fly" + 船 "boat, ship") — the same nautical metaphor that English reaches for in "spaceship," both languages independently borrowing a seafaring vessel to describe travel through a vast, uncharted medium.

examples.hanzi: 宇航员乘坐飞船回到了地球。
examples.pinyin: Yǔhángyuán chéngzuò fēichuán huí dào le dìqiú.
examples.english: The astronauts returned to Earth aboard a spacecraft.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影里有一艘很大的飞船。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ yǒu yì sōu hěn dà de fēichuán.
examples.english: This movie features a very large spaceship.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
宀 (roof) — a house or shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; a hand 寸 under a roof means guarding.
寸 (hand, inch) — originally a hand, as in 对, 寻, 封.

example.hanzi: 他的政治观点比较保守。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhèngzhì guāndiǎn bǐjiào bǎoshǒu.
example.english: His political views are relatively conservative.
example.fact: 保守 works as a verb ("to guard, preserve," 保守秘密 "to keep a secret") and as an adjective ("conservative," 保守派 "conservatives") — the verb sense of protecting something as it is came first, and the adjective sense of resisting change grew out of it, a semantic drift English's own word "conservative" also went through.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷的想法比较保守。
examples.pinyin: Yéye de xiǎngfǎ bǐjiào bǎoshǒu.
examples.english: Grandpa's way of thinking is rather conservative.

examples.hanzi: 请替我保守这个秘密。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng tì wǒ bǎoshǒu zhège mìmì.
examples.english: Please keep this secret for me.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 维 is a rope that holds things together.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) is only a loose sound clue for wéi, as in 推 tuī and 谁 shéi.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.

example.hanzi: 这个国家一直努力维持和平。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā yìzhí nǔlì wéichí hépíng.
example.english: This country has always worked hard to maintain peace.
example.fact: 维持 combines 维 ("a connecting thread or fiber," silk radical 纟) with 持 ("to hold," hand radical 扌) — a thread held taut is the image behind 维持's core sense of keeping something from slackening or falling apart, whether it's peace, order, or a relationship.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要维持良好的身体状态。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào wéichí liánghǎo de shēntǐ zhuàngtài.
examples.english: We need to maintain a good physical condition.

examples.hanzi: 他的工资只能维持一家人的生活。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gōngzī zhǐ néng wéichí yì jiā rén de shēnghuó.
examples.english: His salary can only support his family's living.
